raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Overview

Fixes the first problem reported in #61206: with an engine-based Qwen3 reasoning parser, the reasoning-only pass (`skip_tool_parsing=True`) removes literal think markers quoted inside a tool parameter value before the tool pass sees the span. The forwarded argument must remain verbatim, while a tool opener merely mentioned in reasoning prose must not suppress the real reasoning/content boundary.

## Claims

- In the reasoning-only pass, a skipped tool span is forwarded to the tool pass verbatim: non-tool terminals inside it emit their text instead of applying their reasoning-channel transitions.
- Both `<think>` and `</think>` quoted in tool arguments survive the reasoning pass.
- Qwen3's duplicate-`</think>` absorb in CONTENT still applies outside the span; only in-span handling changes.
- A `<function=...>` opener mentioned in reasoning prose does not open a skipped span or swallow the following real `</think>`.
- No change to normal (non-skip) parsing, streaming deltas, or generation.

## Validation

The reproducers run through the same chain the serving layer uses: a reasoning pass with `skip_tool_parsing=True`, followed by the tool pass on the forwarded content.

```bash
pytest tests/parser/engine/test_engine.py::TestSkipToolParsingMarkerPassthrough \
  "tests/parser/engine/test_qwen3.py::TestNonStreaming::test_think_marker_quoted_in_parameter_survives_reasoning_pass" \
  "tests/parser/engine/test_qwen3.py::TestNonStreaming::test_tool_opener_mentioned_in_reasoning_does_not_hold_content"
```

- The marker-passthrough regressions fail on main and pass on the final head.
- The reviewer-provided tool-opener-in-reasoning case is also a real red/green regression: the intermediate head returned the real `</think>` and subsequent prose as reasoning; the final head restores the expected reasoning/content split.
- Final head: `pytest tests/parser/engine/`: **5868 passed**.
- Pre-commit passes on all three files changed by the final review follow-up.
- Parser-level validation only: this machine has no GPU, so no served-model run. The gate sits in the skip pass and cannot affect sampling or kernels; generated text is unchanged, only the forwarding of already-generated text is repaired.

## Details

Root cause: in `StreamingParserEngine._on_terminal`, the `skip_tool_parsing` gate intercepts tool terminals and tracks `_in_skipped_tool_span`, but any other terminal with a transition reachable from CONTENT still went through `_apply_transition` inside the span. For qwen3 that is `(CONTENT, THINK_END) -> (CONTENT, ())`, the rule that absorbs a duplicate `</think>`. Models can quote think markers as ordinary text inside string arguments, and the absorb deleted them from the text handed to the tool pass.

Fix: while `_in_skipped_tool_span` is set and the terminal is not one of the config's tool terminals, emit the value for the current state instead of applying the transition. Tool terminals keep their existing span-tracking path, so openers and the exit that clears the span behave exactly as before. An intermediate attempt also treated a tool terminal with no transition in the current state as an opener; that was removed after review because it incorrectly captured tool syntax mentioned in reasoning prose. The change lives in the engine rather than `qwen3.py` because the skip pass promises verbatim forwarding for every declarative config.

Relation to nearby open PRs (checked before opening):

- #60256 keeps a text-spelled marker as content in non-streaming parse when it arrives as ordinary tokens; it does not cover a marker token inside a skipped tool span.
- #56661 defers a quoted `<tool_call>` opener in prose; this is the opposite direction, a marker inside an already-open span.
- #58407 balances `</parameter>` closers inside values within the tool parser; this fix is in the reasoning pass that runs before it.

The second problem in #61206 (finish_reason) already has #58286; the third (out-of-order tool results against an ID-less template) is a separate design question, left out of this PR.

nodes.body:
Done, thanks for the pointer. I added a `(CONTENT, THINK_START) -> REASONING` transition to `_absorb_marker_tool_config` and a <think> inside the quoted tool argument to the span text, so `test_think_start_inside_skipped_span_forwarded_verbatim` now covers the case you described. It asserts the whole span is forwarded as text with no `REASONING_START`, which is the behavior this PR fixes.

`tests/parser/engine/test_engine.py` passes (51 tests).

Good catch, and it went further than a missing tag. Those markers were not merely cosmetically lost: the tests were passing without exercising anything.

The grammar's start marker had become an emoji instead of the real one, and the two end markers in the fixtures were empty, so the config and the input never agreed on a marker and nothing in those tests reached the skip path. With the markers put back, all three failed.

What the corrected cases actually show is a real gap in the change I was claiming to make. Span tracking only started when a tool terminal had a transition in the current state. A tool opener reached from reasoning, which has no transition for it, never set `_in_skipped_tool_span`, so the suppression that is supposed to keep markers inside a skipped span from firing their own channel never engaged. A quoted end marker inside the call closed reasoning in the middle of the span:

```text
input:   reason<think><tool_call>alpha </think> omega</tool_call></think>
main:    REASONING_END fires at the </think> inside the call
this:    whole input forwarded verbatim, one REASONING_END at the end
```

`521a9a8e45` sets the flag for a tool opener in the no-transition branch too, which is where the span was being lost. With that the suppression already in `_on_terminal` covers the rest, and the whole call including its quoted markers rides the reasoning channel untouched.

The three tests are rewritten to assert what the change actually promises: the reasoning channel forwards the input verbatim and the only `REASONING_END` lands on the last character. Two of them fail without `521a9a8e45`. The third has no marker inside its span, so it covers the forwarding path rather than this fix, and I would rather say that than let it look like three independent proofs.

Verification on this head: `tests/parser/engine/test_engine.py` is 51 passed, `ruff format --check` is clean on both files, and `ruff check` has one pre-existing `ISC004` at line 204 that is not mine and that I left alone.

Your two suggestions were the right shape. I applied the marker spelling and rewrapped the comment past 88 columns, though I ended up rewriting the assertions rather than taking the second block wholesale, because once the markers were real the `TEXT_CHUNK` comparison no longer described the behaviour.

Dropped the `streaming_parser_engine.py` no-transition opener branch in `b9ad415d1e` and restored the two `_TEXT` cases to the `8215c4cf66` shape. The new `<think>`-in-argument case remains.

I added your exact Qwen3 example as a separate regression. It was red before this follow-up because the real `</think>` and subsequent prose stayed in reasoning; it now returns `reasoning='I could call <function=get_weather> here.'` and `content='\n\nIt is sunny.'`. The quoted-marker repro still reaches the tool pass intact.

Final validation: full `tests/parser/engine/` gives 5868 passed, and pre-commit passes on all three touched files.

## Claude Code Review

This pull request is from a fork — automated review is disabled. A repository maintainer can comment `@claude review` to run a one-time review.

Thanks for working on this. I think the fix works.

I found it also fixes a worse case on DeepSeek V4/V4.1, Gemma4, PLaMo3 and MiniCPM-V, where a start marker like `<think>` inside an argument sends the rest of the call to `reasoning` on main. Could you cover it by adding a `(CONTENT, THINK_START) -> REASONING` transition to `_absorb_marker_tool_config` and a `<think>` to `_TEXT`?
Thanks for adding it. I think the `<think>` tags got lost on the way.

Thank you, and sorry for the confusion. My first comment asked you to add a `<think>` to `_TEXT`, which was unclear. What I meant was a call that opens from content after `</think>` and has a `<think>` in its arguments.

The `_TEXT` tests now put `<tool_call>` inside reasoning instead, where this grammar has no tool call. I think the engine change in 60259b1fec that makes them pass breaks reasoning that just mentions a tool opener, since the real `</think>` after it gets suppressed. With `--reasoning-parser qwen3`:

```text
input:   <think>I could call <function=get_weather> here.</think>\n\nIt is sunny.
main:    reasoning='I could call <function=get_weather> here.'  content='\n\nIt is sunny.'
this PR: reasoning='I could call <function=get_weather> here.</think>\n\nIt is sunny.'  content=None
```

minimax_m2 and deepseek_v4 do the same with their invoke openers.

Could you drop the `streaming_parser_engine.py` part of 60259b1fec and restore those two tests as in 8215c4cf66?

issue_comments.body:
Done, thanks for the pointer. I added a `(CONTENT, THINK_START) -> REASONING` transition to `_absorb_marker_tool_config` and a <think> inside the quoted tool argument to the span text, so `test_think_start_inside_skipped_span_forwarded_verbatim` now covers the case you described. It asserts the whole span is forwarded as text with no `REASONING_START`, which is the behavior this PR fixes.

`tests/parser/engine/test_engine.py` passes (51 tests).

Good catch, and it went further than a missing tag. Those markers were not merely cosmetically lost: the tests were passing without exercising anything.

The grammar's start marker had become an emoji instead of the real one, and the two end markers in the fixtures were empty, so the config and the input never agreed on a marker and nothing in those tests reached the skip path. With the markers put back, all three failed.

What the corrected cases actually show is a real gap in the change I was claiming to make. Span tracking only started when a tool terminal had a transition in the current state. A tool opener reached from reasoning, which has no transition for it, never set `_in_skipped_tool_span`, so the suppression that is supposed to keep markers inside a skipped span from firing their own channel never engaged. A quoted end marker inside the call closed reasoning in the middle of the span:

```text
input:   reason<think><tool_call>alpha </think> omega</tool_call></think>
main:    REASONING_END fires at the </think> inside the call
this:    whole input forwarded verbatim, one REASONING_END at the end
```

`521a9a8e45` sets the flag for a tool opener in the no-transition branch too, which is where the span was being lost. With that the suppression already in `_on_terminal` covers the rest, and the whole call including its quoted markers rides the reasoning channel untouched.

The three tests are rewritten to assert what the change actually promises: the reasoning channel forwards the input verbatim and the only `REASONING_END` lands on the last character. Two of them fail without `521a9a8e45`. The third has no marker inside its span, so it covers the forwarding path rather than this fix, and I would rather say that than let it look like three independent proofs.

Verification on this head: `tests/parser/engine/test_engine.py` is 51 passed, `ruff format --check` is clean on both files, and `ruff check` has one pre-existing `ISC004` at line 204 that is not mine and that I left alone.

Your two suggestions were the right shape. I applied the marker spelling and rewrapped the comment past 88 columns, though I ended up rewriting the assertions rather than taking the second block wholesale, because once the markers were real the `TEXT_CHUNK` comparison no longer described the behaviour.

Dropped the `streaming_parser_engine.py` no-transition opener branch in `b9ad415d1e` and restored the two `_TEXT` cases to the `8215c4cf66` shape. The new `<think>`-in-argument case remains.

I added your exact Qwen3 example as a separate regression. It was red before this follow-up because the real `</think>` and subsequent prose stayed in reasoning; it now returns `reasoning='I could call <function=get_weather> here.'` and `content='\n\nIt is sunny.'`. The quoted-marker repro still reaches the tool pass intact.

Final validation: full `tests/parser/engine/` gives 5868 passed, and pre-commit passes on all three touched files.

Thanks for working on this. I think the fix works.

I found it also fixes a worse case on DeepSeek V4/V4.1, Gemma4, PLaMo3 and MiniCPM-V, where a start marker like `<think>` inside an argument sends the rest of the call to `reasoning` on main. Thanks for adding it. I think the `<think>` tags got lost on the way.

Thank you, and sorry for the confusion. My first comment asked you to add a `<think>` to `_TEXT`, which was unclear. What I meant was a call that opens from content after `</think>` and has a `<think>` in its arguments.

The `_TEXT` tests now put `<tool_call>` inside reasoning instead, where this grammar has no tool call. I think the engine change in 60259b1fec that makes them pass breaks reasoning that just mentions a tool opener, since the real `</think>` after it gets suppressed. With `--reasoning-parser qwen3`:

```text
input:   <think>I could call <function=get_weather> here.</think>\n\nIt is sunny.
main:    reasoning='I could call <function=get_weather> here.'  content='\n\nIt is sunny.'
this PR: reasoning='I could call <function=get_weather> here.</think>\n\nIt is sunny.'  content=None
```

minimax_m2 and deepseek_v4 do the same with their invoke openers.

Could you drop the `streaming_parser_engine.py` part of 60259b1fec and restore those two tests as in 8215c4cf66?
